thesis: Adjusted EPS growth of 23% excluding investment effects gives the bull actual earnings evidence alongside high margins and low leverage. The bear identifies unresolved incremental capex returns but does not overturn the established quality-growth case.
strongest_counterexample: FCF is about half snapshot profit, so large AI investments may deliver accounting growth without commensurate distributable returns.
invalidation_conditions: Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of non-positive year-on-year adjusted EPS growth.
Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of negative FCF.
evidence_gaps: Discrete-item normalization and incremental infrastructure cash returns.
Underlying statement periods and forward-estimate dates are not fully supplied.
decisive_factors: Cloud growth and operating profitability support a quality-growth case
Adjusted EPS growth strengthens the business thesis and cannot be dismissed because capex is high
